data.claim: The add-time duplicate check (check_add -> similar.assess) is wired into lesson_add, decision_add and bug_found, so filing two near-duplicate lessons refuses the second until answered -- it is not agent-discretion (the bug B6d06739825 premise is REFUTED).
data.falsifier: Filing two near-duplicate lessons on current main SILENTLY creates a second lesson record (exit 0) instead of refusing (exit 3) with the first as a candidate.
data.mechanism: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py check_add is called before every add writes; ddflow/services/similar.py assess() scores candidates and on_match=ask refuses a near-duplicate until answered new/extends/duplicate_of/merge_into/related.
data.probe_output: 1 passed -- the second near-duplicate lesson is refused (exit 3) with candidate lesson-1; near-duplicate lesson-2 is NOT in state.lessons until answered --new
data.question: Does the record-filing path (lesson add / bug found / decision add) already run the semantic duplicate check automatically, so a near-duplicate is refused instead of silently filing a second record?
